approaches.name: national electronic vaccination data system for registration and digital certificates
approaches.description: The EVDS records COVID-19 vaccinations nationally, alerts recipients to doses and issues digital certificates, interoperating across provincial systems. Practices: electronic vaccination data system (EVDS) for vaccination tracking; Electronic Vaccination Data System for COVID-19 rollout; EVDS vaccination registration, alerts and digital certificates; Electronic Vaccination Data System (EVDS) for COVID-19 rollout; Electronic Vaccination Data System for national vaccine rollout; EVDS national interoperable vaccination records across provinces.

evidence.text: An important innovation has been the establishment of an electronic vaccination data system (EVDS), which serves a similar purpose to the EU’s digital green pass and an important step toward a robust e-health system (see also Prior Action 4, Section IV). b.

extra_evidence.text: Prior Action 4: To improve equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines, the Borrower, through its National Department of Health, has launched the South African COVID-19 Programme Registration, which introduces the use of an Electronic Vaccination Data System (EVDS), compliant with the applicable data protection and privacy legislation, in the rolling-out of the Borrower’s COVID-19 vaccination program, setting the stage for future health emergencies, as further evidenced in the COVID-19 Implementation Guide and Toolkit.
The February 2021 shift toward a new electronic vaccine data system (EVDS) has been a critical element in the country’s transformation to a digital health system.
Results: The system is designed to: (i) capture the relevant metrics of all South African residents who will be vaccinated;

(ii) ensure vaccinees are contactable and alerted to optimize adherence to the vaccination regime; and (iii) complete the certification process such that vaccine certificates are easy to obtain for those vaccinated and authorities that may require the certification.

approaches.name: online grant applications with automated cross-database eligibility checks
approaches.description: Digital applications and monthly automated cross-checks against tax, employment, identity and banking databases verify eligibility and flag duplicate applicants. Practices: online portal for wage-subsidy applications with public recipient transparency website; digital social grant application with automated eligibility cross-checks; monthly real-time database cross-checks for grant eligibility; cross-programme digital cross-checks to detect double-dipping; electronic application and automated cross-checking for social grants.
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: online application plus public recipient disclosure - cue: 'piloted' | category Operational; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The firms apply for the funds each month through an online portal, receive the grants through direct deposit to bank accounts, and are required to pay out the grant to their employees.

extra_evidence.text: It has launched a transparency mechanism—all firm recipients are named through an online website—to provide workers with information to monitor their own receipt of funds and has developed grievance procedures, including independent investigators, to follow up on employee and employer complaints.
681, which introduce the use of electronic means to allow for digital application procedures and automated cross-checking to verify eligibility.
The new directive makes it possible to use digital technologies in the identification of beneficiaries, distribution of cash payments, and monitoring to reduce leakages.

SASSA developed a protocol for a fully digitalized process to deliver the COVID-19 SRD grant and built a new system with the appropriate capacity to import data from other institutions to carry out cross-checks in a fraction of the time that it normally takes to process these data.

Importantly, the eligibility of grant recipients is cross-checked against several linked databases (including SARS, UIF, student bursary fund, home affairs, government employment records, other grant databases, and banking institutions) monthly to ensure recipients are not collecting other social benefits or have had any other status changes affecting their eligibility.
The enhanced and real-time eligibility verification ensures that 4.6 million ineligible applicants were quickly identified and avoids payments being made to those who do not qualify.

The real-time cross-check of eligibility is an Page 27 The World Bank South Africa COVID-19 Response Development Policy Operation (P174246) important policy enhancement compared with how other social grants are managed and an efficiency innovation that is expected to generate important fiscal savings through the improved targeting of payments.
The digital protocols that introduced cross- checks across social programs to ensure no double-dipping were re-instituted and improved in 2021 to better monitor eligibility and reduce leakage.

The system detected 4.6 million ineligible applicants, of the 14 million original applications in August and September, namely individuals who were already registered with the UIF, received other social grants, were on the Government’s payroll system, did not match information in the home affairs database, were duplicate applications, or otherwise did not meet the COVID-19 SRD grant eligibility criteria.
As a result, the program avoided paying R 11.2 billion (US$744 million) to ineligible applications in September 2021.

approaches.name: multi-channel digital SRD grant registration with real-time application tracking
approaches.description: Applicants register via WhatsApp, USSD, email, website, Facebook or GovChat and track applications in real time.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: multi-channel digital enrolment with live application tracking - cue: 'USSD' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: With the re-introduction of the COVID-29 SRD grant in August 2021, all applicants to the program are required to register through WhatsApp, USSD line, email, the SASSA website, Facebook, or GovChat (an online platform connecting the Government and citizens).

extra_evidence.text: Because of the digital enrolment, the application trail was immediately established and gave beneficiaries real-time tracking of their applications at each stage without visiting SASSA offices, using call centers, or dealing with lost reference-number receipts, which provides better customer service and reduces administrative costs.
The digital footprint reduces the time and cost of the appeal process as well, allowing for just-in-time cross-checks against live databases that determine eligibility.
